resale_co.name: Land/Structure Compliance (Certificate of Occupancy) inspection
resale_co.issued_by: Construction, Zoning and Code Enforcement Office (Dept. of Construction Enforcement)
requirements: Walks and driveways free of trip hazards
Yard free of weeds and debris, grass cut
House number at least 4 inches high, visible from the street
Paint not peeling or cracking, no untreated wood exposed
Service entry cable, gutters, downspouts, decks, steps and building exterior (foundation, walls, roof, glazing, basement hatch) in good condition; 3 or more risers need a graspable rail
Floor coverings without trip hazards; walls and ceilings in good condition
Smoke alarm within 10 feet of bedrooms and on every level including the basement; CO alarm within 10 feet of all sleeping rooms
Fire extinguisher 2A:10B:C, 10 lb maximum, mounted in the kitchen, visible and readily accessible, top no more than 5 feet above the floor
Graspable rails on all stairs including the basement
Bathrooms have an operable window or a fan exhausting outside
GFCI protection on outlets within 6 feet of a sink and in the garage, basement and outside
A light fixture in every hallway, interior stairway, bathroom, kitchen, laundry room, boiler or furnace room and basement
Plumbing fixtures working with hot and cold water and no visible leaks; water heater relief valve discharge within 6 inches of the floor
Gas appliances vented with combustion air and clearances; dryer vented outside with metal flex duct; washer drains to the drain system
Door locks meet code (no double keyed locks); at least one insect screen in every room

fees.label: Reinspection appointment when smoke/CO alarms or extinguisher fail (older notice on page 2 of the same form, dated 2007)
fees.quote: EFFECTIVE 6/14/2007, FAILURE TO HAVE WORKING SMOKE DETECTORS, CARBON MONOXIDE DETECTORS AND FIRE EXTINGUISHER WILL REQUIRE AN ADDITONAL FEE OF $15 FOR A REINSPECTION APPOINTMENT.

resale_co.how_to_apply: Fill out the Land/Structure Compliance Application (posted as 'Application Certificate of Occupancy' on the Construction, Zoning & Code Enforcement page) with the property use, occupancy, lockbox code, seller, agent, buyer, settlement date and whether the home will be rented, and submit it with the fee to the Construction Office (the form lists City Hall, 1 W. New Jersey Avenue; the web page lists 741 Shore Road), 9:00 am to 5:00 pm weekdays. The office-use section takes cash or check and records any open permits.

resale_co.notes: The City's Land/Structure Compliance Application (the 'Application Certificate of Occupancy', updated 4/14/23) asks for seller, agent, buyer and settlement date, charges $250.00 per dwelling unit, and its checklist is titled 'Requirements for all resale and rental inspections'. The form does not quote the ordinance that makes the inspection mandatory and the City Code on ecode360 could not be opened, so confidence is medium. Page 2 of the same scanned form carries an older notice (effective 6/14/2007) of a $15 reinspection appointment fee when smoke/CO alarms or the extinguisher fail; the current $100 reinspection fee on page 1 may supersede it. The form's footer address (City Hall, 1 W. New Jersey Avenue, 609-927-9088 ext. 142) differs from the web page's Construction Office address (741 Shore Road). Other office staff: Roe Howell, Technical Assistant to the Construction Official, (609) 927-9088 ext. 148, rhowell@spgov.org. The form also asks whether the home will be a short-term (under 175 days) or long-term rental; rental licensing is a separate program.

requirements: State online self-certification, now named the Certificate of Smoke Alarm, Carbon Monoxide Alarm, and Secondary Power Source Identification Label Compliance (CSACMASPSIL): smoke alarms, carbon monoxide alarms, and the secondary power source label for homes with solar, generators or batteries. The certificate name no longer includes the fire extinguisher, although the portal's checklist notice still refers to detectors and fire extinguishers

The City's resale inspection form (2023) also checks smoke alarms, CO alarms and a 2A:10B:C extinguisher of 10 lb or less mounted to the kitchen wall, and notes 10-year sealed lithium battery smoke alarms have been required since 1/1/2019 (existing hardwired alarms excepted)

authorities.how_to_apply: Apply online through the NJ DCA Fire Safety portal ('Start Your Smoke Certification Application'). Pay by e-check or credit card before submitting; a valid email address is required. The certificate is emailed once the application is submitted, the fee is paid and any required inspections are done. Homes heated by electricity with no CO alarm requirement should also email BFCE_CSDCMAC@dca.nj.gov.

fire_cert.notes: The City says it no longer has a Bureau of Fire Prevention and that the service is provided by the State, and the state fire directory lists 'NJ Division of Fire Safety' for smoke detector compliance in Somers Point. However, the DCA's July 17, 2026 list of State-enforced towns shows Somers Point without the 'SC' (smoke certs) flag that it gives most other State-enforced Atlantic County towns, so it is not certain the DCA online certificate is the right one here. The City's own resale Land/Structure Compliance inspection also checks smoke alarms, CO alarms and the extinguisher. Confidence is low until someone confirms who issues the smoke/CO certificate for a Somers Point sale. The directory gives (609) 633-6132 for Louis Kilmer; the Bureau's own page gives (609) 633-6106, which is used here.

other_items.label: Open permits

open_questions: Who issues the smoke/CO certificate for a Somers Point sale: the NJ DCA online portal (the City says the State provides fire inspection service), or the City's own resale inspection? DCA's 7/17/2026 list does not mark Somers Point 'SC'.
Lead time before closing and how long the Land/Structure Compliance certificate stays valid are not stated.
Whether the 2007 $15 smoke/CO reinspection fee on page 2 of the form still applies alongside the $100 reinspection fee.
